title: Model registry indexer + metadata broker to publish runtime-aware profiles
creator: Maya Patel
description: We need a lightweight indexer + metadata broker that converts model onboarding artifacts into a stable, queryable runtime profile surface. This ticket defines the API contract and server-side adapter that will publish: published_version (semver-like), supported_context_range (min,max tokens), token_cost_estimates (per-token and per-embedding), feature_flags (tool-calling, streaming, structured-output), kv_cache_hints (warmup_prefixes, cacheable_prefix_fraction), quantization_recommendations (quant-types, expected_latency_mul), and affinity_hints (kernel_affinity, preferred_cuda_compute_capability). The goal is to expose these fields via a versioned HTTP endpoint so serving layers (hosted/dedicated/private) can route & pin safely and UIs can surface realistic limits and cost estimates.
acceptance_criteria: A /v2/registry/index/{model_id} endpoint returns a stable profile JSON string for model versions with documented schema version
Profiles include min/max context, token cost estimate, supported features, and suggested runtime knobs (batching/quantization)
Serving runtime can consume the published profile to perform safe version pinning and fallback decisions
Backward-compatibility notes included so older runtimes ignore new fields without failing
Integration tests that validate schema evolution and example consumer behavior (fallback to compatible model variant)
backwards_compat_notes: Schema uses schema_version field; consumers must ignore unknown top-level keys. New numeric fields are non-breaking additions. If published_version is missing, consumers should treat entry as pre-onboarding and fall back to heuristics. We include a short deprecation policy: fields may be removed only after two full release cycles and a migration window announced in registry metadata.
